`*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n100\t/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n101\t/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n102\t/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n103\t/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\n104\tfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n105\t    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n106\t    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n107\t        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n108\t    }\n109\t\n110\t    let mut result = String::new();\n111\t    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n112\t    let mut i = 0;\n113\t\n114\t    while i < chars.len() {\n115\t        match chars[i] {\n116\t            '\\\\' => {\n117\t                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n118\t                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n119\t                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n120\t                    result.push('\\\\');\n121\t                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n122\t                    i += 2;\n123\t                } else {\n124\t                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n125\t                    result.push('\\\\');\n126\t                    i += 1;\n127\t                }\n128\t            }\n129\t            '*' => {\n130\t                // Check for **.\n131\t                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n132\t                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n133\t                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n134\t                    i += 2;\n135\t                } else {\n136\t                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n137\t                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n138\t                    i += 1;\n139\t                }\n140\t            }\n141\t            c => {\n142\t                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n143\t                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n144\t                // the glob conversion.\n145\t                result.push(c);\n146\t                i += 1;\n147\t            }\n148\t        }\n149\t    }\n150\t\n151\t    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n152\t    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n153\t}\n154\t\n155\t/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n156\t///\n157\t/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n158\t/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n159\t///\n160\t/// # Arguments\n161\t///\n162\t/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n163\t/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n164\t/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n165\t///\n166\t/// # Returns\n167\t///\n168\t/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n169\t/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n170\t///\n171\t/// # Examples\n172\t///\n173\t/// ```\n174\t/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n175\t/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n176\t///\n177\t/// let rules = vec![\n178\t///     RoutingRule {\n179\t///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n180\t///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n181\t///     },\n182\t///     RoutingRule {\n183\t///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n184\t///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n185\t///     },\n186\t/// ];\n187\t///\n188\t/// // First rule matches.\n189\t/// assert_eq!(\n190\t///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n191\t///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n192\t/// );\n193\t///\n194\t/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n195\t/// assert_eq!(\n196\t///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n197\t///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n198\t/// );\n199\t/// ```\n200\tpub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n201\t    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n202\t    for rule in rules {\n203\t        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n204\t            Ok(compiled) => {\n205\t                if compiled.matches(model) {\n206\t                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n207\t                }\n208\t            }\n209\t            Err(e) => {\n210\t                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n211\t                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n212\t                tracing::warn!(\n213\t                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n214\t                    error = %e,\n215\t                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n216\t                );\n217\t            }\n218\t        }\n219\t    }\n220\t\n221\t    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n222\t    if default.is_empty() {\n223\t        None\n224\t    } else {\n225\t        Some(default.to_string())\n226\t    }\n227\t}\n228\t\n229\t/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\n230\t///\n231\t/// This is a lower-level function that tests if a glob pattern matches a model name.\n232\t/// It uses the `glob` crate's Pattern type directly for glob-style pattern matching.\n233\t///\n234\t/// # Arguments\n235\t///\n236\t/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n237\t/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n238\t///\n239\t/// # Returns\n240\t///\n241\t/// * `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\n242\t/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\n243\t///\n244\t/// # Edge Cases\n245\t///\n246\t/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n247\t/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\n248\t/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n249\t///\n250\t/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n251\t///\n252\t/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n253\t/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n254\t/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n255\t/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n256\t/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n257\t///\n258\t/// # Examples\n259\t///\n260\t/// ```\n261\t/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n262\t///\n263\t/// // Match with wildcard\n264\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n265\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n266\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n267\t///\n268\t/// // Match with double wildcard\n269\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n270\t///\n271\t/// // Edge cases\n272\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n273\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n274\t/// ```\n275\tpub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n276\t    // Handle edge cases\n277\t    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n278\t        return None;\n279\t    }\n280\t\n281\t    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n282\t    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n283\t        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n284\t            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n285\t            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n286\t                Some(())\n287\t            } else {\n288\t                None\n289\t            }\n290\t        }\n291\t        Err(_) => {\n292\t            // Invalid glob pattern\n293\t            None\n294\t        }\n295\t    }\n296\t}\n297\t\n298\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n299\t// Tests\n300\t// Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// ];\n///\n/// // First rule matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n/// );\n///\n/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\n///\n/// This is a lower-level function that tests if a glob pattern matches a model name.\n/// It uses the `glob` crate's Pattern type directly for glob-style pattern matching.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\n/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n///\n/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n///\n/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n///\n/// // Match with wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n///\n/// // Match with double wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n///\n/// // Edge cases\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n    // Handle edge cases\n    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n                Some(())\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            // Invalid glob pattern\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n/// );\n///\n/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\n///\n/// This is a lower-level function that tests if a glob pattern matches a model name.\n/// It uses the `glob` crate's Pattern type directly for glob-style pattern matching.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\n/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n///\n/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n///\n/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n///\n/// // Match with wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n///\n/// // Match with double wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n///\n/// // Edge cases\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n    // Handle edge cases\n    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n                Some(())\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            // Invalid glob pattern\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\n///\n/// This is a lower-level function that tests if a glob pattern matches a model name.\n/// It uses the `glob` crate's Pattern type directly for glob-style pattern matching.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\n/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n///\n/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n///\n/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n///\n/// // Match with wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n///\n/// // Match with double wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n///\n/// // Edge cases\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n    // Handle edge cases\n    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n                Some(())\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            // Invalid glob pattern\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character -
